figures.caption: Fig. 1: Semantic classes and their distribution for a representative participant (Subject 1), which is almost consistent across all subjects.
Fig. 2: Overview of the proposed Semantic Alignment Framework.

Fig. 4: Classification performance of the task-optimized closed-set classifier and the proposed contrastive EEG–language framework across Subjects 01– 05. Results are reported as the mean ± std across the five held-out crossvalidation folds.

Fig. 6: Top-1 and Top-5 accuracy among the held-out test trials retained by validation-derived MaxCosine thresholds for Subject 01. The horizontal axis reports the achieved held-out test coverage. Points and error bars represent the mean ± standard deviation across the five folds.

TABLE III Illustrative held-out Top-5 decoding examples across validation-referenced MaxCosine percentiles for Subject 01. Percentiles express each test score relative to its fold-specific validation-score distribution. A higher percentile therefore indicates a higher relative MaxCosine score, not a calibrated probability of correctness.
Fig. 8: Fold-specific ROC curves for discrimination of correct and incorrect Top-1 predictions using raw MaxCosine for Subject 01.

Fig. 9: Balanced accuracy measures agreement between the semantic-axis assignment derived from the held-out EEG embedding and that derived from the corresponding sentence embedding. Bars show the mean across the five subjects and error bars indicate the standard deviation across subjects. The dashed line denotes the 50% chance level.

Fig. 10: SGP example for Subject 1. A frozen gallery of held-out sentence embeddings is projected to 2D via PCA for visualization. Each point corresponds to a gallery sentence and is colored by its cosine similarity to the EEG trial.
